cards.text: The LORD has just said He will ruin the pride of Judah and Jerusalem (Jeremiah 13:9). Now the message to them opens with “Listen and give heed. Do not be arrogant…” Then it tells them WHY.

cards.question: Why are the people of Judah told not to be arrogant?

answers.text: Because the king has commanded it

cards.text: Next the message says, “Give glory to the LORD your God before He brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the dusky mountains.” Friend, that’s hiking down a mountain at sunset when your phone flashlight dies at 1 percent.

cards.question: The message says the people wait for light, but the LORD turns it into deep gloom and thick darkness.

cards.text: Then the message says what will happen if they don’t listen. And this is where you see a heart breaking for them.

cards.question: If the people of Judah don’t listen, what does the speaker in the message say will happen?

answers.text: Weeping in secret because of their pride
Leaving Jerusalem and never coming back
No more bringing them the LORD’s word

cards.question: The message says, “My eyes will overflow with tears.” Why?

answers.text: The LORD’s flock has been taken captive
The temple has been torn to the ground
The king has turned the city against them

cards.text: Now a message goes ALL the way to the top: to the king and to the queen mother.

cards.question: The king and the queen mother are told to take a ___ seat, because their glorious crowns have fallen from their heads.

cards.text: From glorious crowns to a lowly seat, that’s first class to the seat by the restroom, and there is NO upgrade coming. And it’s not just the palace: the cities of the Negev, down in Judah’s south, have been shut tight, and no one can open them.

cards.question: The message says only a few towns of Judah have been carried into exile.

cards.text: The message keeps going, and now it’s a call to look up. Lift up your eyes, it says, and see who’s coming.

cards.question: The message says to lift up your eyes and see who’s coming. From which direction are they coming?

cards.text: Then comes a hard question: “Where is the flock entrusted to you, the sheep that were your pride?” That’s the dog sitter when the owner walks in, looks around and says, “So… where’s Max?”
And then: “What will you say when He sets over you close allies whom you yourself trained?” That’s training the new guy at work, and a month later he’s your BOSS.

cards.question: The message asks whether pangs of anguish won’t grip them, as they do a woman in ___.

cards.text: Then the message sees the next question coming: “Why has this happened to me?” And it answers it straight.

cards.question: The answer to “Why has this happened to me?” is that their enemies were simply too strong for them.

cards.text: It’s because of the magnitude of their iniquity that their skirts have been stripped off and their body exposed. Then comes the famous line: “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?”

cards.question: “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?” What is that question saying about the people?

answers.text: They can’t do good when they’re used to evil
They will change once the trouble comes
They are no worse than the other nations

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: “I will scatter you like chaff driven by the desert wind.” That’s cookie crumbs on my counter with the ceiling fan on HIGH, and friend, you are NOT finding all of them.

cards.question: The LORD says this is their lot, the portion He has measured to them, because they have ___ Him and trusted in falsehood.

cards.text: So He will pull their skirts up over their face, that their shame may be seen. Then He names their adulteries and lustful neighings, their shameless prostitution on the hills and in the fields.

cards.question: The LORD says He has seen Jerusalem’s detestable acts.
The LORD says, “Woe to you, O Jerusalem!” Then He asks Jerusalem a question. What does He ask?

answers.text: How long it will remain unclean
Why it went back to Egypt
